findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py lines 874-882, the OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative offsets when enable_advanced_features is True. However, Django ORM slicing with negative offsets is not standard and can lead to unexpected behavior or errors. The comment claims the ORM handles negative slicing automatically, but Django QuerySets do not support negative start indices in slicing. This can cause runtime exceptions or incorrect query results when negative offsets are used.
findings.suggestion: Replace negative offset slicing with an alternative approach, such as reversing the queryset and using positive offsets, or explicitly handling reverse pagination without negative indices.
findings.title: Negative offset slicing in queryset is unsupported and unsafe

findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py lines 68-93, the new 'optimized_pagination' query parameter enables the OptimizedCursorPaginator only if the user is superuser or has global access. However, the check uses 'organization_context.member.has_global_access' without verifying if 'organization_context.member' is not None, which can cause an AttributeError if member is None.
findings.suggestion: Add a check to ensure 'organization_context.member' is not None before accessing 'has_global_access', e.g., 'organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access'.
findings.title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None

findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py lines 888-892, the logic for trimming results when cursor.is_prev and cursor.value is present uses 'len(results) == offset + limit + extra' to decide whether to drop the last item. However, 'offset' can be negative in OptimizedCursorPaginator, which may cause incorrect length comparisons and slicing errors.
findings.suggestion: Use the actual expected length (limit + extra) for comparison instead of 'offset + limit + extra' to avoid errors with negative offsets.
findings.title: Incorrect length check when trimming results with negative offsets in OptimizedCursorPaginator

models.summary: This change adds an OptimizedCursorPaginator with support for negative offsets and advanced pagination features, and integrates it into the organization audit logs endpoint for authorized users. However, it introduces a critical bug by using negative slicing on Django QuerySets, which is unsupported and can cause runtime errors. Additionally, there are potential attribute access errors and incorrect length checks related to negative offsets that need fixing.
